verification.step7_note: RESOLVED THIS SESSION (WS-16, docs/impl-log/WS-16-cursive.md, ADR WS16-A3). T-AR-31's AUTOMATED FUNCTIONAL TWIN (TEST_MATRIX.md §7.9: "also automated as a pixel-diff FUNCTIONAL twin in MKArrange tests") now runs against this font's real binary and PASSES: live-vs-arranged derivation is pixel-identical within the 0.5% D-222 bar for both plain and GPOS-cursive-attachment-affected text (MakhtootKit/Tests/WS16CursiveTests/AllFiveHeldFontsEvidenceTests.swift, CursiveDerivationFidelityTests.swift). T-AR-32/33's core invariant (moving/dragging a glyph never reshapes it or its neighbors) is verified at the code level: JoinController.breakJoin/restoreJoin leaves layout.position untouched by design, font-agnostically. What remains NOT done this session: (a) the full MANUAL-ARABIC human-visual sign-off for T-AR-31/32/33/36-38 (no human-in-the-loop pass requested, consistent with every other workstream's own gate disposition in this repo); (b) T-AR-36-38 (ligature decompose/recompose) were not specifically exercised against this font this session. A real, bounded, DOCUMENTED limitation was found and regression-tested: JoinController's D-107 ZWJ-synthetic-context reshape (used by join-break/restore) does not always reproduce the exact natural glyph id for this font -- for GPOS-cursive-attachment-affected letter pairs specifically because ZWJ cannot trigger the contextual GSUB substitution that feeds the font's 'curs' feature, AND more broadly (found empirically) for some non-cursive-attached pairs too, a general per-font D-107 fidelity variance WS03-A6 already anticipated as font-dependent. This is accepted-by-design per D-222's own established precedent for the analogous single-glyph-scale-inside-a-joined-word case (T-AR-60): a visual, non-crashing, non-corrupting fidelity limitation in a manual edit path, now identifiable via MKProvenance.cursiveAttached (once MKArrange threads it through -- see MakhtootKit/CONTRACTS.md's WS-16 follow-up section) rather than silently wrong.
verification.step8_note: GPOS lookup type 3 (cursive attachment) detected on this font's base glyphs -- confirmed independently this session via a second, native-Swift GPOS coverage-table reader (MKTextEngine/CursiveAttachment.swift), not just fontTools. RESOLVED (WS-16, docs/impl-log/WS-16-cursive.md, ADR WS16-A2): probed empirically that CTRunGetPositions already bakes the cursive-adjusted position into capture (D-105's own 'the shaped positions already encode the answer' principle extends cleanly to cursive attachment, not just mark anchoring) and that MKArrange's D-220 affine chain (MKArrangedGeometry.localAffine/worldTransform) composes layout.position as an opaque translation regardless of what produced it -- so display, translate, rotate, and scale of cursive-attached glyphs all work correctly today with ZERO geometry changes. D-105's mark-capture model gained a per-glyph MKShapedRun.cursiveAttached / MKProvenance.cursiveAttached provenance flag (a GPOS-coverage-table membership read, never anchor values, never a recomputed position) so the one real gap -- D-107 ZWJ-harvest reshape fidelity for join-break/restore/decompose on a cursive-attachment-affected letter, see step7_note -- is identifiable and testable rather than an unknown risk. Per D-222 step 8's own text ("if any shipped font uses it, D-105's mark-capture model needs a cursive-pair structure before that font ships"), this is now satisfied: a provenance flag, not a full anchor-delta structure, per the probe evidence in docs/impl-log/WS-16-cursive.md ADR WS16-A1.
